topic: Comptroller and Auditor General — mixed tiers
description: CAG of India: appointment, tenure, role, key reports

questions.stem: The COMPTROLLER + AUDITOR GENERAL (CAG) of India is appointed by:

options.option_text: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
Lok Sabha by passing a resolution

questions.explanation: Article 148 — CAG appointed by PRESIDENT (under his hand and seal). Tenure: 6 YEARS or until age 65 (whichever earlier). Salary + service conditions DETERMINED BY PARLIAMENT — same as a Supreme Court Judge. Not eligible for further govt office after retirement (to ensure independence). Removed only by impeachment-like process (proved misbehaviour or incapacity, by both Houses with special majority — same as SC judge). Ambedkar called CAG 'most important officer of the Constitution' alongside Election Commission.

questions.topic: Comptroller and Auditor General — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The CAG is mentioned in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 148-151 deal with CAG. 148: appointment, oath, conditions of service. 149: duties + powers. 150: form of accounts. 151: audit reports submitted to PRESIDENT, who lays them before Parliament. CAG is INDEPENDENT (like SC judge); accountable to Parliament (not executive). Audits all CONSOLIDATED FUND of India + states + UT (with legislatures) + CONTINGENCY FUND + PUBLIC ACCOUNT. Distractor 1 = Money Bills (Speaker's certification). Distractor 3 = Finance Commission. Distractor 4 = Election Commission.

questions.stem: The CAG's report is submitted by him/her to the:

options.option_text: Finance Minister of the Govt of India
Chairperson of the Public Accounts panel

questions.explanation: Article 151 — CAG submits AUDIT REPORTS to the PRESIDENT, who CAUSES THEM TO BE LAID before each House of Parliament. CAG submits to GOVERNOR for state-level reports → laid before state legislature. Once tabled, reports go to PUBLIC ACCOUNTS COMMITTEE (PAC) — joint committee of MPs, chaired by an Opposition MP (convention since 1967) — examines audit findings, summons officers, recommends action. PAC is one of 3 'Financial Committees' of Parliament: PAC, Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU), Estimates Committee.

questions.stem: The CAG's TERM of office (or maximum age) is:
questions.explanation: CAG = 6 years OR retires at 65 — whichever comes first. Single non-renewable term. After retirement, NOT eligible for further govt. office (to preserve independence). Removed only by parliamentary procedure similar to Supreme Court Judge: special majority resolution in both Houses on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. Salary CHARGED on Consolidated Fund of India (not subject to vote of Parliament — to safeguard).

questions.stem: Which CAG audit famously exposed the '2G SPECTRUM' allocation losses (2010)?
questions.explanation: VINOD RAI (CAG 2008-2013) — high-profile reports: 2G SPECTRUM (2010, presumptive loss of ₹1.76 lakh crore in spectrum allocation by 2008 telecom minister A. Raja); COALGATE (2012, presumptive loss in coal block allocation, ~₹1.86 lakh crore); CWG 2010 (audit of irregularities). Reports led to: PIL → SC cancelled 122 telecom licenses (2012) + coal block allocations (2014); A. Raja arrested. Politically consequential — fueled UPA-2 anti-corruption narrative. Successors: Shashi Kant Sharma (2013-17), Rajiv Mehrishi (2017-20), Girish Chandra Murmu (2020-).

questions.stem: CAG audits the accounts of which of the following?
questions.explanation: CAG audits: (1) CENTRAL government — all ministries + departments (Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account); (2) STATE governments (similar); (3) PSUs (Public Sector Undertakings) — both central + state — supplementary audit alongside private chartered accountants under Companies Act; (4) AUTONOMOUS BODIES + corporations substantially financed by government (e.g., AIIMS, IITs, IIMs, ICAR); (5) certain GRANTS to specific schemes / NGOs. CAG does NOT audit private companies. CAG = principal AUDITOR of the country.

questions.stem: The CAG of India is sometimes called the 'GUARDIAN OF THE PUBLIC PURSE' because the office:

options.option_text: Audits all spending from the Consolidated Fund
Sets monetary policy with the RBI

questions.explanation: Public Purse = Consolidated Fund of India. CAG audits all withdrawals + ensures spending was AUTHORISED by Parliament + done LAWFULLY + ECONOMICALLY. Three types of audit: (1) FINANCIAL — accounts accurate; (2) COMPLIANCE — rules followed; (3) PERFORMANCE — value for money, efficiency. CAG cannot stop spending (only audits AFTER); but reports + parliamentary follow-up ensure accountability. INDIA's audit institution is part of INTOSAI (International Org of Supreme Audit Institutions). Distractor 3: budget approved by Parliament; CAG audits the spending.
